validity.recommendation: Keep the row; it is a real, distinct gas line. Add a Status/Fuel ref (staged). Resolve the owner and diameter concerns filed below.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — confirmed. The line appears in the Egypt Oil & Gas 'Western Desert' feature PDF (the sheet's sole cited source) inside the table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert', row 'Salam-Matruh Terminal' with Length 75 km / Diameter 10 in / Capacity 22 mmcf/d — the GEM values are a faithful transcription of that table (len 75, dia 10, cap 22 all match exactly). That is one source, but GulfPub PE World Map independently lists an operating gas line 'Salam - Matruh' (Salam field -> Matrouh), and OGJ/Offshore-Technology confirm the Salam gas plant on Apache's Khalda concession supplies gas/LPG to Matruh Governorate. Two-plus independent traces => existence solid. CLASSIFICATION — gas transmission, defensible: the Egypt O&G table is explicitly 'Natural Gas Infrastructure' and GulfPub tags it operating gas; it is a small (10 in / 22 mmcf/d) trunk carrying processed gas from the Salam plant toward the Marsa Matruh area (city/governorate supply), not a plant-internal or oil line. DUPLICATE — none. It is distinct from the other Salam/Matruh roster rows: P6693 Salam Spurline (35 km / 22 in / 250 mmcf/d, table row 'Salam Spurline'), P0476 Salam-Abu Gharadig Southern (212 km / 18 in / 187, table row 'Salam-Abu Gharadig', actually ->Abu Gharadig not Matruh), and the Badr El Din spurs P3937/P3938 (Badr El Din Field->Matruh). GulfPub 'Salam - Matruh' is the external counterpart of THIS row, not a separate GEM entity. Only support for the sheet is the one Egypt O&G PDF (8 backlinks all trace to it), so per-field corroboration is limited — see the spec/attribution concerns.

validity.recommendation: Change Owner1 from 'General Petroleum Co' to Khalda Petroleum Company (JV of Apache Corp + EGPC; EGAS also holds an interest). Decide owner-vs-operator: Khalda operates the Salam system; ultimate owners are EGPC/Apache. General Petroleum Company (GPC) is a Gulf-of-Suez EGPC affiliate and almost certainly a mis-entry here.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists Owner1 = 'General Petroleum Co' 100%. This is almost certainly wrong. The Salam field and Salam gas plant sit on Apache's Khalda concession and are operated by Khalda Petroleum Company (KPC), a JV of Apache Corporation and EGPC, with EGAS also holding an interest — confirmed independently by Oil & Gas Journal ('KPC is a joint venture company of Apache Corporation and Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC)') and Offshore Technology, and by GulfPub which attributes the 'Salam - Matruh' line to Khalda Petroleum Company. 'General Petroleum Company' (GPC) is a separate EGPC affiliate operating chiefly in the Gulf of Suez / Eastern Desert, not the Western Desert Khalda acreage — so the current owner is a likely name confusion. Note the whole Egypt Western-Desert gas family transcribed from the same Egypt O&G PDF may share this owner error; worth a class check.

validity.recommendation: Treat Diameter=10 in and Capacity=22 mmcf/d as single-source (Egypt O&G) and low-confidence; do NOT upgrade to green. Diameter conflicts with GulfPub (16 in) — flag for a second source before trusting either. Length 75 km is corroborated by geometry; keep.
validity.researcher_notes: Diameter 10 in and Capacity 22 mmcf/d both come ONLY from the Egypt O&G Western Desert table (the sheet's single source). GulfPub independently gives Diameter 16 in and Length 52 km for its 'Salam - Matruh' line (its Capacity_mmcfd=300 is the known placeholder, not a real value), so DIAMETER is in direct conflict (10 vs 16, ~38% delta) and unresolved on two independent sources. No third source found stating a diameter or capacity for this specific line. LENGTH 75 km, by contrast, is well supported: the Salam gas plant (~30.71N, 26.98E) to Marsa Matruh (~31.35N, 27.25E) is a ~75 km straight-line corridor, matching GEM exactly; GulfPub's 52 km looks short. So: keep Length (medium/high), but Diameter and Capacity stay low-confidence single-source with an open diameter conflict.

routes.start_name: Salam gas plant (Khalda concession, Western Desert, Matruh Governorate)
routes.end_name: Marsa Matruh area (Matruh Terminal / city-supply receiving point on the Mediterranean coast)
routes.corridor_desc: Runs roughly NNE from the Salam gas processing plant in the Khalda concession (northern Western Desert) across the open desert of Matruh Governorate to the Mediterranean coast at/near Marsa Matruh. Straight-line separation is ~75 km, matching the GEM length; the actual routed path is unmapped, so the corridor is bounded by the two endpoints only. End point 'Matruh Terminal' is the coastal receiving/city-gate point serving Matruh Governorate.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from sources: OGJ/Offshore-Technology/oilandgasadvancement place the Salam gas plant on Apache's Khalda concession in the northern Western Desert and describe it supplying gas/LPG to Matruh Governorate; GulfPub gives the line as Salam field -> Matrouh. Marsa Matruh city coordinate (31.3525N, 27.2453E) is a well-known place. The Salam gas plant coordinate (30.7097N, 26.9769E = 30 42'35"N 26 58'37"E) is taken from a public map (Wikimapia) lead, NOT an authoritative source — flagged as approximate; it is corroborated only in that the resulting ~75 km straight-line matches the GEM/Egypt O&G length. No coordinates were fabricated; intermediate waypoints are unknown so none are given, and the corridor is left loosely bounded (suggested accuracy low).

summary: P3935 real & correctly gas-classified (Egypt O&G + GulfPub), distinct from other Salam/Matruh rows; but Owner 'General Petroleum Co' is wrong (should be Khalda Petroleum Company / Apache-EGPC) and Diameter 10 in conflicts with GulfPub 16 in (single-source); Length 75 km corroborated by geometry.
